selectionRationale: All tokenizer references and all hash-bound retrieval judgments passed, including the three cross-language positive pairs.
Independent Python ONNX Runtime reference vectors matched with cosine similarity above 0.9999999999998 and maximum absolute difference below 1.1e-7 on all registered references.

The pair is operationally heavier than native MiniLM/Core ML and MLX, but it is the only measured compact pair with complete tokenizer, vector, multilingual-retrieval, and packaging-path evidence in this qualification pass.
Measured performance is recorded as Pareto evidence, not an invented product hard gate.

alternatives.reason: Passed the small casebook with the smallest model/runtime footprint and lower measured RSS, but no independent reference vector is yet registered for its pinned upstream Core ML export. It remains the leading simplification candidate for a future requalification.
Passed the casebook but was slower and used materially more peak RSS than the all-compute native Core ML configuration; independent vector parity also remains open.

Fastest measured pair with the lowest E5 runtime RSS, but its vectors were nearly orthogonal to the independent reference and it missed the Chinese-to-English anonymous-credentials retrieval judgment. A future maintained conversion may be requalified as a new candidate.

Matched reference vectors and retrieval, but only 562 of 623 nodes were accepted across 38 Core ML partitions; repeated unbounded-shape conversion failures, CPU fallback, higher latency, lower throughput, and 14.7 GB measured peak RSS make this configuration unsuitable.
Retained for tokenizer parity, but it is not independently a maintained encoder execution runtime and Crosscurrent will not build a bespoke tensor engine.
The compact candidates did not expose a casebook quality ceiling that justifies this larger conditional candidate.
The compact candidates did not expose a casebook quality ceiling that justifies this substantially larger conditional candidate.

releaseLimitations: No representative slower or baseline M1-class Apple-silicon Mac was available; this host does not establish baseline-device performance.
Repeated local runs may benefit from filesystem cache; the measured cold-start value is process initialization on the recorded host, not a cold-disk guarantee.

The official ONNX Runtime distribution is a thin arm64 dylib; final framework/dylib embedding, hardened-runtime signing, notarization, Sparkle update, rollback, and third-party-notice packaging remain release gates.
The current machine has no valid signing identity, so production selection and signed-archive qualification remain pending.
